item.description: Long before grunge made Seattle famous, Chris Cornell had already picked his local musical heroes. Among British rock influences, there was one American band he saw as a standout.

item.title: FOO FIGHTERS Release 'TODAY’S SONG' Ahead of Album’s 30th Anniversary; VIDEO
item.description: Foo Fighters have released a new track titled “Today’s Song” (watch below) to celebrate the upcoming 30th anniversary of their self-titled debut album. The single is available now on major streaming platforms.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Confirms Live Retirement: 'It’s A Goodbye As Far As My Live Performances Go'
item.description: In a new interview promoting this weekend’s Back to the Beginning event, the legendary Black Sabbath frontman confirmed that his upcoming concert at Villa Park in Birmingham, England, will be his final time performing live.

item.title: The Disgusting Reason Metallica's JAMES HETFIELD Hates LOAD and RELOAD Album Covers
item.description: Metallica’s mid-’90s albums, Load and Reload, are remembered for more than just a shift in musical style. Their cover art caused a stir too, especially with frontman James Hetfield.

item.title: The AC/DC Album Fans LOVE to HATE Isn’t as BAD as You Remember
item.description: In the early 1980s, AC/DC was riding high. The back-to-back success of Highway to Hell (1979), Back in Black (1980), and For Those About to Rock (We Salute You) (1981) turned the band into a global powerhouse.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD Hated The Direction Metallica Took In The ‘90s: 'So Stupid'
item.description: In a 2001 interview with Playboy, Metallica frontman James Hetfield reflected on the band’s major style shift during the Load era. For Hetfield, that period, complete with designer clothes, makeup, and fashionable haircuts, wasn’t exactly a high point.

item.title: EVANESCENCE Hits No. 1 on Rock Chart for the First Time With 'Afterlife'
item.description: Evanescence has reached a major milestone. The band has scored its first-ever No. 1 song on Billboard’s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart with “Afterlife”, their latest single featured in the Netflix series Devil May Cry (watch below).

item.title: The Song That Annoyed JAMES HETFIELD, but METALLICA Covered Anyway: 'It Drove Me Nuts'
item.description: James Hetfield has built a career on intensity and control, but even he has moments where personal taste takes a back seat. One of those moments came in the late 1990s, when Metallica recorded “Turn the Page” for their 1998 cover album Garage Inc.

item.title: BLACK SABBATH’s Founding Four Reunite Ahead of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final Show; First Photos Released
item.description: The original members of Black Sabbath have reunited to rehearse for one last performance. Ozzy Osbourne, Geezer Butler, Tony Iommi, and Bill Ward are preparing for their farewell event, “Back To The Beginning: Ozzy’s Final Bow”, which takes place on July 5 at Villa Park in Birmingham, England.

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Responds to Criticism With Instagram Post: 'It's Never F-cking Good Enough'
item.description: Asking Alexandria has drawn attention again, this time through a post on their official Instagram. The band shared a video clip of frontman Danny Worsnop performing the song “Things Could Be Different” during their recent Warped Tour appearance in Washington, D.

item.title: The Song JAMES HETFIELD Considers the Greatest of All, and Countless Bands Have Tried to Recreate
item.description: James Hetfield has always worn his influences on his sleeve. In a recent episode of The Metallica Report (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), the Metallica frontman named Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven” as the greatest song of all time.

item.title: Why One of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Old Rivals Agreed to Play at BLACK SABBATH’s Farewell Show
item.description: Jake E. Lee hasn’t spoken to Ozzy Osbourne in decades. The two didn’t exactly part ways on good terms, and there’s been little reason for contact since Lee was fired back in the ’80s.

item.description: In an interview with Rolling Stone in 2021, guitarist Angus Young opened up about a moment that split fans of AC/DC, when Axl Rose stepped in as lead singer during their 2016 tour.

item.title: AC/DC Opens European Tour in Prague, Czech President Attends; VIDEOS
item.description: AC/DC launched the summer leg of their “Power Up” European tour Thursday night in Prague, Czech Republic. The concert took place at Letiště Praha Letňany and drew an estimated crowd of 60,000 people.

item.description: For a band known for thrash, fire, and a habit of rattling stadium foundations, Metallica’s transformation didn’t happen with a single riff or overnight revelation. It was a slow burn.

item.title: AC/DC Adds More Australian Shows As Fans Struggle With Ticket Website Issues
item.description: AC/DC has added three new dates to its upcoming Power Up tour in Australia. The new shows are scheduled for: November 16 in Melbourne at Melbourne Cricket Ground November 25 in Sydney at Accor Stadium December 18 in Brisbane at Suncorp Stadium Fans can find tickets and all official dates at acdc.

item.title: HALESTORM Releases New Music Video for 'DARKNESS ALWAYS WINS': 'Evil Prevails And The Good Depart First'
item.description: Halestorm has unveiled a new official video for “Darkness Always Wins,” the band’s first release of 2025 (watch it below). Directed by DJay Brawner and produced by Dave Cobb, the song builds slowly with a cinematic tone and sits firmly in the band’s hard rock catalog.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Says He Wants To Work With PAUL MCCARTNEY: 'I Would Be Honoured'
item.description: During a new episode of Ozzy Speaks on SiriusXM (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Ozzy Osbourne mentioned that he would like to collaborate with Paul McCartney. The rock icon discussed the idea while chatting with his co-host, Billy Morrison.

item.title: WOLFGANG VAN HALEN Explains Why He Backed Out of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final Concert: 'I Wouldn’t Be Able To Pull It Off'
item.description: Wolfgang Van Halen, son of late guitar legend Eddie Van Halen, was originally scheduled to appear at Ozzy Osbourne’s farewell concert, Back to the Beginning, on July 5 in Birmingham, U.

item.description: Tom Morello is playing a key role in organizing Black Sabbath’s last concert. And for him, one name was essential: Jake E. Lee, the guitarist who played with Ozzy Osbourne in the 1980s.

item.title: The Band EDDIE VAN HALEN Believed Saved Rock ‘n’ Roll From Extinction: 'Rock Wouldn’t Exist Without Them'
item.description: Rock music has had plenty of supposed saviors. Every few decades, someone new gets the credit for dragging the genre back from the brink. Eddie Van Halen was one of those names, but according to him, his own rise might not have happened without a much earlier band shaking things up.

item.title: Metallica's KIRK HAMMETT Recalls Struggling With 'The Unforgiven': 'I Wasn't Prepared For It'
item.description: Metallica guitarist Kirk Hammett is known for writing some of the band’s most famous guitar parts, but not every one came easy. In a recent interview with Metal Hammer, he opened up about the difficulties he faced while working on the solo for “The Unforgiven”, one of the standout tracks from the band’s 1991 self-titled release, often called “The Black Album.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Honored With New 'Working Class Hero' Display in Hometown
item.description: A new exhibition honoring Ozzy Osbourne is now open in his hometown of Birmingham, England. The “Working Class Hero” exhibit launched Wednesday (June 25) at the Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery.

item.title: Mick Ralphs, Co-Founder of Bad Company and Mott the Hoople, Dies at 81
item.description: Mick Ralphs, the guitarist and songwriter who helped shape the sound of classic rock with Bad Company and Mott the Hoople, has died at age 81. He is survived by his partner, Susie Chavasse, his two sons, three stepchildren, and his longtime bandmates Paul Rodgers and Simon Kirke.

item.description: Before joining Led Zeppelin and becoming a rock legend, John Bonham was already turning heads in the music scene of England’s Black Country. As a teenager, just 16 years old, he crossed paths with a fellow drummer: Bill Ward, who would later power Black Sabbath’s thunderous rhythm section.

item.title: Watch FEMME FATALE's New Video for 'Living Like There's No Tomorrow'
item.description: Femme Fatale, the rock band led by Lorraine Lewis, has returned with a new song called “Living Like There’s No Tomorrow” (watch it below). The track is now available through Cleopatra Records, and its official music video, directed by Vicente Cordero, is out now.

item.title: AC/DC Faces Backlash Over Viral Tour Footage As Fans Call For Retirement: 'Painful'
item.description: Footage from a recent AC/DC concert is making waves online, and not in the way the band might hope. A TikTok video from the group’s May 4 performance at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, has gone viral (watch it below).

item.description: Black Sabbath is officially preparing for its final show with original singer Ozzy Osbourne. The band shared a new photo of Ozzy, bassist Geezer Butler, and drummer Bill Ward in a rehearsal studio (See the photo at the end of the article).

item.title: JAKE E. LEE Asks Fans Not To Judge OZZY OSBOURNE’s Performance: 'He Deserves This Farewell'
item.description: Guitarist Jake E. Lee is urging fans to show compassion ahead of Back to the Beginning, the farewell concert for Ozzy Osbourne and the original Black Sabbath lineup.

item.title: The RUSH Album That Led to Fan Backlash, Internal Tension, and a Moment of Regret: 'It Wasn’t the Smartest Move'
item.description: Most bands with long careers eventually take a creative detour. Whether to keep things fresh or avoid burnout, they try something new. Sometimes it works. Sometimes it doesn’t.

item.title: SEBASTIAN BACH Talks Dimebag Darrell’s Wild Hotel Incident: 'He Stabbed The Couch On Acid'
item.description: Sebastian Bach recently shared a wild story from his days on tour with Pantera. The former Skid Row frontman opened up in a new interview about a chaotic moment involving the late Dimebag Darrell, a knife, and a hotel lobby couch (via Sense Music Media) (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.

item.title: Creed's SCOTT STAPP On Viral Revival: 'It Started Online Before We Even Noticed'
item.description: Scott Stapp says the Creed reunion didn’t start with a grand plan or a flashy PR campaign. It began with the internet doing its thing. In a recent interview (via Meltdown), the singer explained that the band started to see signs of renewed interest around 2020, when clips, memes, and jokes about Creed started to go viral.

item.title: AC/DC Announces 2025 Stadium Tour of Australia With Amyl and The Sniffers
item.description: AC/DC is heading back to their roots. The legendary Australian rock band has announced a five-city stadium tour across the country for November and December 2025. This will be their first Australian tour in ten years.

item.title: The AC/DC album that FLOPPED HARDER Than Expected And Nearly Turned Into A FULL-BLOWN CRISIS
item.description: Back in Black is the album everyone knows. It’s the one that sold like crazy and turned AC/DC into a global powerhouse. But not every album had the same luck.

item.title: SCOTT STAPP Says CREED Is Rebuilding: 'We're Talking About New Music'
item.description: CREED frontman Scott Stapp says the band is easing back into things after more than a decade apart. In a recent interview, he shared that the group has been spending time together, reflecting on the past, and having early conversations about making new music (via Meltdown) (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: THE BAND That Toured With Guns N’ Roses and Wished They Hadn’t: 'I Don’t Want To Be Around Them'
item.description: In the early ’90s, opening for Guns N’ Roses was considered a golden ticket, massive crowds, media buzz, and a shot at mainstream fame. For Soundgarden, a loud and rising band from Seattle, the offer felt like a fast pass out of the grunge underground.

item.title: The Night SLASH Felt Deep Shame Over GUNS N’ ROSES’ Treatment of METALLICA: 'I Lost Their Respect'
item.description: Back in the early ’90s, Guns N’ Roses were living the full-throttle rockstar fantasy, loud, chaotic, and unapologetic. Their shows were wild, their image untamed, and their reputation built on pushing limits.

item.title: The Emotional METALLICA Song That Wasn’t Meant to Be, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: When Load dropped in June 1996, it marked a sharp left turn for Metallica. The band traded speed and aggression for a slower, more reflective sound. That shift didn’t land well with everyone, but it did show fans a broader side of the band’s musical identity.

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Fans Question Danny Worsnop’s Performance, Call for His Exit
item.description: Asking Alexandria’s recent Warped Tour performance is stirring debate online, and some fans think it may be time for lead singer Danny Worsnop to step aside. The band’s subreddit lit up after their June 15 set, with over a dozen posts and hundreds of comments discussing Worsnop’s vocals and stage presence.

item.title: The Unusual Way AC/DC's ANGUS YOUNG Came Up With the Chorus of 'HIGHWAY TO HELL'
item.description: Angus Young, lead guitarist and founding member of AC/DC, shared a rather unexpected story about how he wrote one of rock’s most iconic choruses. Speaking in a 2021 interview with Essentials Radio on Apple Music (via Kerrang), Young explained how the chorus of “Highway to Hell” came to him, not in a studio or during rehearsal, but while he was on a bathroom break.

item.title: The 'COMMERCIAL' Song AC/DC Didn’t Want To Record, And It Ended Up On The Charts
item.description: In June 1978, AC/DC got their first taste of chart action in the UK with “Rock ’n’ Roll Damnation”, which reached number 24. Nothing to throw a parade over, but for a band that had never cracked the charts there before, it was a decent showing.

item.title: The AC/DC Song They’d Rather Pretend NEVER HAPPENED: 'Really Soft Stuff'
item.description: “But the answer was literally on the other side.” Back when AC/DC hadn’t yet locked in the sound that would make them gods to some and repetitive to others, they were still fumbling through the dark.

item.title: 5 METALLICA Songs That Have Nothing to Do With HEAVY METAL, Yet WORKED BRILLIANTLY
item.description: Say heavy metal and Metallica instantly comes to mind. Since the early ’80s, the band carved out the sound, fury, and attitude of a genre that lives off shrieking guitars and bone-rattling drums.

item.title: THREE DAYS GRACE Releases New Single 'DOMINATE' Ahead Of Upcoming Album
item.description: Three Days Grace has released a new single titled “Dominate” (watch the video at the end of the article), available today on all major streaming platforms. The track is part of the band’s upcoming eighth studio album, Alienation, scheduled for release on August 22, 2025, via RCA Records.

item.title: The One AC/DC Song ANGUS YOUNG Struggles to Play Live
item.description: Few bands are as famously built on no-nonsense riffs as AC/DC. For Angus Young and his brother Malcolm, there was no mystery to their formula: loud guitars, open chords, and choruses made for the crowd to scream in unison.

item.description: Back when rock was drowning in mousse and tight pants, Nirvana kicked down the door like a grunge-splattered SWAT team. Metallica? They’d already been tearing limbs off with thrash riffs from the Bay Area for a decade.

item.description: Sharon Osbourne still hasn’t let it go. Two decades after the absolute circus that was Ozzfest 2005, she’s perfectly willing to laugh about sabotaging Iron Maiden with beans, pre-recorded sound effects, and strategic sound cuts.

item.title: "Thunderstruck," AC/DC Classic, Featured in FIFA Club World Cup Commercial
item.description: AC/DC’s Thunderstruck is the soundtrack for Budweiser’s new commercial. The beer company is a sponsor of the FIFA Club World Cup, which features 32 teams and is currently being held in the United States.

item.title: AC/DC Reportedly Planning Final Concerts For Late 2025 In Australia
item.description: According to behind-the-scenes information obtained by Blunt magazine, AC/DC is expected to announce what could be the final concerts of their career, scheduled for late 2025 (Get AC/DC Tickets Here).

item.description: Fifteen years after dropping their debut Feel The Steel, Steel Panther is still out there doing what they do best: mocking, exaggerating, and somehow keeping hair metal alive with a straight face and a wink.
